Where Dreams Meet Destiny

Written by Bhat Arfinda

THE BOOK

Foreword

Some stories are born from imagination, while others emerge from the deepest corners of the human heart. Some begin with a dream, others with a struggle, and a few with a destiny that no one could ever have predicted.

Where Dreams Meet Destiny is a journey through the beautiful yet complicated dimensions of life. It is a story about a girl who dares to dream in a world that constantly reminds her of her limitations. A girl who refuses to let circumstances define her worth, who carries countless aspirations in her heart, and who believes that somewhere beyond the boundaries of her little world, a different life awaits her.

But life is rarely as simple as the dreams we create.

Sometimes, the road to achieving our ambitions is filled with sacrifices, unexpected encounters, and moments that change the meaning of everything we once believed in. Sometimes, destiny introduces people into our lives when we least expect them, turning ordinary moments into unforgettable memories.

This story is not merely about love, nor is it solely about the pursuit of dreams. It is about courage, resilience, sacrifice, and the unpredictable nature of destiny.

It reminds us that a person can achieve everything they once wished for and still discover that life has its own plans.

As you turn these pages, allow yourself to enter Aaliya's world. Witness her struggles, understand her dreams, and walk beside her as life unfolds in ways she could never have imagined.

Because some journeys are not remembered for how they end, but for everything they make us feel along the way.

And perhaps, somewhere between dreams and destiny, you may find a part of your own story.

THE BOOK

Preface

Every story has a beginning, but not every story begins on paper. Some stories begin quietly, deep within the heart, long before they find their way into words.

Where Dreams Meet Destiny is one such story.

I did not begin writing this book merely to create a fictional world or entertain readers. I began writing it because there are emotions, experiences, dreams, and realities that sometimes deserve more than silence. There are things we experience, things we observe, and things we carry within ourselves that cannot always be explained through ordinary conversations. Sometimes, writing becomes the only way to give those feelings a voice.

At the heart of this novel is Aaliya, a girl whose journey is shaped by ambition, hardship, determination, love, and destiny. Through her, I wanted to explore the struggles of a girl who dreams of a life beyond the boundaries imposed upon her. Aaliya...... who wishes to discover the world, build her own identity, and prove that her circumstances do not have the authority to decide her future.

Although Aaliya is a fictional character, many of the emotions and underlying experiences reflected in her journey are deeply personal to me. In some ways, writing her story has also been a way of expressing parts of my own life — the dreams I have carried, the realities I have witnessed, and the feelings that words often struggle to describe.

As the story unfolds, it moves beyond the pursuit of dreams and enters the unpredictable world of human connections, unexpected encounters, and love. It explores how life can bring people together in the most unexpected circumstances and how even the most beautiful moments can become precious memories.

I want readers to understand that this is not simply a story about a girl who falls in love. It is about a girl who first learns to dream, then finds the courage to pursue those dreams, and eventually discovers that destiny has its own way of writing the chapters of our lives.

I have tried to give every chapter its own emotion, every character a purpose, and every moment a meaning. My hope is that readers will not simply read Aaliya's journey but will feel connected to it.

Perhaps you will recognise her courage, understand her silence, relate to her ambitions, or find a reflection of your own experiences somewhere within these pages.

I do not know what every reader will take away from this book. But I hope that when you reach its final page, you will pause for a moment and think about the dreams you once held close to your heart and the unpredictable journey that life has written for you.

After all, we spend our lives chasing dreams, believing that destiny will eventually lead us somewhere beautiful.

ABOUT THE WRITER

Bhat Arfinda is a writer whose words are deeply connected to emotions, dreams, experiences, and the realities of life.

Where Dreams Meet Destiny is more than just a work of fiction. In many ways, it is a reflection of the writer's own inner world — a story shaped by personal experiences, unspoken emotions, distant dreams, and the determination to create a life beyond the limitations of circumstances.

Behind the character of Aaliya lies a part of the writer's own journey. Her dreams represent the aspirations that have lived quietly within the writer's heart; her struggles echo the realities that have shaped a perspective on life; and her determination reflects the belief that one's circumstances should never be allowed to define one's destiny.

For the writer, storytelling is not simply about creating characters or imagining beautiful moments. It is about giving words to feelings that are sometimes difficult to express, bringing attention to realities that often remain unnoticed, and creating a world in which readers can discover emotions they may recognise within themselves.

Through this book, Bhat Arfinda hopes to remind readers that behind every dream lies a struggle, behind every smile may exist an untold story, and behind every individual is a world that others may never fully understand.

This book carries a piece of the writer's heart — a collection of emotions transformed into words, experiences shaped into a narrative, and dreams given a life of their own.

Because sometimes, the stories we write are not entirely imagined. Sometimes, they are the stories we have lived, the emotions we have carried, and the dreams we have never stopped believing in me.

For everyone who has ever dreamed, hurt, loved, and kept going. Inside these pages, you may find a piece of your own story

"Before you begin this journey, I want to tell you something. Perhaps, somewhere between these pages, you will find a reflection of your own life. Perhaps there will be a moment when you pause and think, this is my story. These are the feelings I've carried. And if that happens, then yes, perhaps this story belongs to you as much as it belongs to me. Aaliya's journey is not just about dreams and destiny. It's about courage, silent pain, and the hope that survives even in the hardest moments. As you read her story, I invite you to celebrate her courage, understand her struggles, and feel the emotions that accompany her along the way. And when you reach the final pages, you may find yourself wishing things had turned out differently. But that's the truth of life, not every beautiful journey ends the way we hope. Some achieve their dreams but cannot keep everything their hearts wish for. If this story touches your heart, reminds you of someone, or brings back a chapter of your own life, know that your feelings are understood. Thank you for allowing Aaliya's story to become a part of yours.

With love,

Bhat Arfinda.

Where Dreams Meet Destiny

A Personal Note from the Author

The Story Behind Where Dreams Meet Destiny

Where Dreams Meet Destiny is not just a fictional story. It is, in many ways, a reflection of my emotions, my experiences, my dreams, and certain realities of my life.

I am Bhat Arfinda, the writer of this book. Through Aaliya's journey, I have tried to express feelings and experiences that I could not always put into words in my own life.

Although some characters and situations in this novel are fictional, the emotional struggles behind Aaliya's childhood, particularly the trauma she experiences because of her father's actions, are inspired by real experiences. Some parts of this story are deeply connected to my own life.

So, if you ever feel that Aaliya's story is somehow my story too, then you are not entirely wrong.

I am currently a Class Twelve student, still studying, still growing, and still working towards my dreams. I wrote this story because I wanted to express my life through words. I wanted to give a voice to emotions that often remain hidden inside a person.

Aaliya represents a girl who never gives up on her dreams. Despite the difficulties she faces, she continues fighting for her education, her independence, and the future she wants to build. She dreams of becoming a doctor, making her mother proud, and creating a life beyond the limitations of her childhood.

She keeps moving forward, even when life gives her countless reasons to stop.

But this story also reminds us of something painful: no matter how big our dreams are, life does not always unfold according to our plans. We can work hard, remain determined, and give everything we have, yet destiny may have a different ending waiting for us.

Aaliya achieves many of her dreams, but her journey ends in a way she never imagined. Her health struggles and the emotional burden she carries become an important part of her tragic journey.

That is why I chose the title Where Dreams Meet Destiny. It represents the moment when our ambitions, hopes, and efforts meet the uncertainty of fate. Sometimes, even when we are ready to live the life we have always dreamed of, destiny takes us somewhere we never expected.

There is another message I wanted to share through this novel: not every man is the same.

Aaliya's experiences with her father make it difficult for her to trust people. She begins to believe that every man might disappoint her. However, Çağrı Baylan's character introduces her to a different kind of person—someone who listens, respects her boundaries, supports her dreams, and treats her with kindness.

I included Çağrı Baylan in this story for a personal reason as well. He is my favorite Turkish actor, and bringing him into this fictional world was something I genuinely wanted to do. His character became an important part of Aaliya's journey, representing the idea that kindness and respect can exist even after someone has experienced betrayal.

Through this novel, I hope readers find something that connects with their own lives. Perhaps someone will recognize their childhood in Aaliya's struggles. Someone else may understand her determination, her mother's sacrifices, her longing for love, or her desire to become independent.

I want readers to feel her journey—not simply read it.

Aaliya never stopped dreaming. She never stopped trying. She continued fighting for the future she wanted, right until the end of her journey. Her story may be fictional in its characters and certain events, but the emotions behind it come from a much more personal place.

I am still following my own dreams. I am still a student, still learning, and still hoping to create the future I have imagined for myself.

Perhaps that is the most personal connection between Aaliya and me: she never gave up on her dreams, and neither do I.

Thank you to every reader who gives this story a chance, understands its emotions, and carries a little part of Aaliya's journey with them.

This book is my way of expressing what words have held inside me for so long.

With love and gratitude,

Bhat Arfinda

Writer of Where Dreams Meet Destiny

CHAPTER

Chapter 1: Behind the Beauty of a Village

There once existed a village of extraordinary beauty, a place where nature seemed to have painted its finest masterpiece. Surrounded by breathtaking landscapes, lush greenery, and an atmosphere of tranquillity, it appeared to be nothing less than a paradise.

But beneath its enchanting beauty lay a dark and deeply concealed secret.

In that village, women were not regarded as individuals with dreams, ambitions, or aspirations. They were treated as though their only purpose in life was to serve others. Education was considered unnecessary for girls, stepping outside the boundaries of their homes was forbidden, and freedom was nothing more than an unfamiliar word.

These beliefs were not merely social expectations; they were traditions that had been passed down through generations.

And then, into this very village, a little girl was born.

Her name was Aaliya.

She was a beautiful, gentle-hearted girl with an extraordinary spark within her. Even at a young age, she possessed something that distinguished her from the world around her: an unquenchable thirst for knowledge, an immense desire to study, and an adventurous spirit that longed to explore the world beyond the familiar boundaries of her village.

She dreamed of discovering places she had never seen, learning things she had never been taught, and experiencing a life that extended far beyond the walls of her home.

Unfortunately, the world she was born into had no room for such dreams.

As the years passed, Aaliya began to understand the harsh realities of her surroundings. She gradually became aware of the restrictions imposed upon girls, the injustice hidden behind the village's traditions, and the silent suffering endured by countless women.

She desperately wanted to distance herself from this suffocating environment. She wanted a different life, a life in which she could make her own decisions and become someone beyond the identity society had assigned to her.

But her struggles had begun long before she could even understand them.

At just six years old, Aaliya had already witnessed more pain than a child should ever have to comprehend.

Her childhood was marked by sacrifices, fear, and countless heartbreaking experiences. The greatest source of her suffering was her own household. Her father, the very person she believed should have been her protector, would often subject her mother to physical a*us*.

Those painful incidents left an invisible scar on Aaliya's young heart. Although she was too little to understand the complexities of adult relationships, she could feel the heaviness of the atmosphere surrounding her family.

Aaliya had two sisters as well, which placed an even greater burden upon her mother. In a society where daughters were considered a responsibility rather than a blessing, her mother was constantly made to feel that having three girls was somehow a disadvantage.

There were days when circumstances became so unbearable that the family went without proper food and even the basic necessities of life. Sometimes, Aaliya found herself confined to a single room, surrounded by silence, uncertainty, and thoughts far too complicated for her tender age.

Yet, despite everything, her mother continued to make sacrifices.

She endured hardships that words could scarcely describe, silently carrying the weight of her family while trying to protect her daughters from a world that had already judged them.

And somewhere within all that suffering, a determination began to take shape in Aaliya's heart.

She wanted to achieve something extraordinary.

She wanted to build a beautiful life for herself, give her mother the happiness she had been deprived of, and prove that being born a girl was never a limitation.

She wanted her mother to experience the life she had never been allowed to live.

However, there was something Aaliya had not yet fully understood about her father.

Despite everything that happened within their household, she believed him to be a good, respectable man. In her eyes, he was not entirely a bad person. She thought his only flaw was his narrow perspective on life, his inability to understand the importance of education, freedom, and a girl's individual identity.

She had yet to discover how complicated the truth could be.

This was only the beginning of Aaliya's journey.

A journey filled with unanswered questions, unspoken pain, extraordinary dreams, and the determination to create a future entirely different from the life she had been born into.

But what awaited Aaliya beyond the boundaries of her village?

Would she ever succeed in changing her destiny?

Or would the traditions of her village become the very chains that prevented her from reaching her dreams?

Only time would reveal the answers.

Her story had only just begun.

CHAPTER

Chapter Two: The Price of a Dream

For Aaliya, the journey towards her dreams did not begin with freedom. It began with sacrifice.

Her mother, despite facing countless difficulties and opposition from her own family, was determined to send her daughters to school. She knew that education was perhaps the only door through which her girls could escape the limitations of the world they had been born into.

Somehow, after enduring arguments, financial difficulties, and endless resistance, she managed to send Aaliya to school.

It was not an easy achievement. For some families, sending a child to school was an ordinary part of life. But for Aaliya's mother, it was a battle she had to fight every single day.

And eventually, she won that little battle.

Aaliya began attending school.

For the first time, she had an opportunity to step beyond the walls that had confined so many girls before her. She could hold books in her hands, learn new things, meet people, and imagine a future that looked different from the life surrounding her.

But her struggles did not end at the school gates.

In fact, a different kind of struggle awaited her every time she returned home.

There were responsibilities, bitter remarks, restrictions, and constant reminders that she was a girl whose education was considered unnecessary.

Her father would often question the purpose of educating daughters.

"What will a girl achieve by studying so much?"

Such remarks were not merely words to Aaliya. They were painful reminders that even her simplest dreams were considered unreasonable by the people around her.

And it was not only her father.

Her paternal grandmother, her uncle, and several other members of the family were also against the idea of educating the girls. Her maternal relatives, however, seemed somewhat different in their attitudes, although Aaliya could never truly know what everyone held in their hearts.

Perhaps some cared more than they could express. Perhaps others had their own reasons for remaining silent.

But one thing Aaliya gradually understood was that she could never completely know what lived inside another person's heart.

Sometimes, one person's opposition is enough to make an entire journey difficult.

And Aaliya had more than one obstacle standing in her way.

Her sisters were struggling too. They were growing up in the same environment, facing the same restrictions and experiencing the same uncertainty about their future.

Yet, even at such a young age, Aaliya was remarkably understanding. She was affectionate, sensitive, and unusually mature for her age. She noticed things that other children might have overlooked. She understood the sadness in her mother's eyes, the tension in the household, and the sacrifices that went unnoticed by everyone else.

She was especially sensitive towards her mother and sisters. Their suffering affected her deeply, sometimes more than she could explain.

Every time she saw her mother struggling, a quiet determination grew stronger within her.

She wanted to become someone her mother could be proud of.

She wanted to give her the happiness she had spent years sacrificing for her daughters.

And so, little by little, Aaliya continued moving towards her dreams.

But one particular morning would leave a memory in her heart that she would never forget.

A Mother's Tears

It was an ordinary evening.

Aaliya was at home when she noticed her mother sitting quietly, tears falling from her eyes. There was something different about her that evening. She looked exhausted, helpless, and lost in her thoughts.

Aaliya slowly approached her.

"Mumma, why are you crying?"

Her mother quickly tried to compose herself, but the sadness in her eyes was impossible to hide.

She looked at Aaliya and spoke in a trembling voice.

"Beta, I don't have any money left. What am I supposed to do now? I have to arrange your uniforms, pay your school fees, and manage everything else. I don't know where I will get the money from. How am I going to manage all of this?"

For a moment, Aaliya remained silent.

She was only a little girl. She did not have a solution to her mother's financial problems, nor did she understand how difficult it was to arrange money when there was barely enough to meet the family's basic needs.

But she knew one thing: she could not bear to see her mother cry.

She gently looked at her and said:

"Mumma, God is there, isn't He? He will make everything alright. Please don't worry. Everything will be fine."

Those were simple words, spoken by a little girl who had very little control over her circumstances.

But sometimes, the smallest words carry the greatest hope.

Her mother looked at her daughter, perhaps finding a little comfort in the innocence of her reassurance.

She only knew that her mother needed hope.

And she wanted to give her some.

That night, Aaliya went to sleep with countless thoughts in her little mind.

She had dreams of studying, growing, and achieving something meaningful. But somewhere deep inside, she also carried a wish that her mother would never have to cry over money again.

The Morning That Broke a Mother's Heart

The following morning arrived.

As everyone slowly woke up, Aaliya's mother began preparing tea for the family. Aaliya was also awake, moving around the household as she usually did.

It was then that something caught her mother's attention.

Her mother-in-law was sitting with a piece of roti in her hand. She was breaking it into several tiny pieces and distributing those pieces among the bowls meant for Aaliya and her sisters.

Beside her, she had kept two or three whole rotis separately.

Aaliya's mother watched this quietly for a moment.

Then, unable to understand the reason behind it, she asked:

"Why are you breaking the rotis into such tiny pieces? And why have you kept those three rotis separately?"

Her mother-in-law answered casually, without appearing to think much about the impact her words might have.

"These little pieces are for your daughters. And these three rotis are for my grandson, Aamir."

Aamir was a young boy, their cousin.

For a few moments, there was silence.

Aaliya's mother could hardly believe what she had just heard.

The same household. The same kitchen. The same family.

Yet the food was being divided differently simply because some children were girls and another was a boy.

Her daughters were being given tiny pieces of bread, while a whole portion had been reserved for their male cousin.

It was not merely about the rotis anymore.

It was about the difference in the value assigned to children. It was about a mother's daughters being treated as though their hunger mattered less.

And perhaps what hurt her most was the realization that this was happening right before her eyes, within the very family that was supposed to treat all its children equally.

Her heart sank.

She had already spent so much of her life fighting for her daughters. She had struggled to educate them, struggled to provide for them, and struggled to protect their childhood.

And now, even something as basic as food had become another reminder of the injustice they were facing.

She looked at the little pieces of roti and then at the three whole ones kept aside for Aamir.

Perhaps she had no words left to express what she was feeling.

And Aaliya, who had been observing the world around her since childhood, was growing up in the middle of these painful realities.

She was still young, but every such incident was quietly teaching her something about the world.

A world in which a girl's dreams could be questioned, her education could be opposed, and even her simplest needs could be treated differently.

But this was not the end of Aaliya's story.

It was only another chapter in the life of a girl who had yet to discover how far her determination could take her.

Her journey had begun, but the world had not yet finished testing her.

To be continued...

CHAPTER

Chapter Three: A Home Divided, A Childhood Shattered

Sometimes, a woman reaches a point in her life where staying becomes more painful than leaving. It is not that she has stopped hoping for things to improve; it is simply that she has begun to understand that her children deserve a life beyond constant suffering.

For Aaliya's mother, that moment had finally arrived.

After enduring countless hardships, humiliations, and unequal treatment, she made a decision that would change the lives of her daughters.

She decided that they would live separately.

It was not a decision made out of anger alone. It was a decision born from years of disappointment, emotional exhaustion, and a mother's determination to protect her children.

She wanted a separate space for herself and her daughters, somewhere they could live without constantly being reminded that they were unwanted or considered less important.

And so, she began separating their belongings.

She collected the utensils, kitchen essentials, and whatever household items belonged to her and her daughters. Slowly, she moved everything into their own little space.

Their arrangement was far from comfortable.

There were six rooms in the house. Two of them became their living space: one room for the girls and their mother, and another that served as their kitchen, where meals were prepared and the little necessities of everyday life were managed.

It was not the kind of home a mother would dream of providing for her children.

But it was the beginning of an attempt to give them something they had rarely experienced before: a separate life.

However, separation did not necessarily mean peace.

Their father refused to live with them.

Instead, he chose to remain downstairs with his parents, his brother, and his brother's wife. He continued his life there, while his wife and daughters were left to manage their own little household separately.

He had, in many ways, left his own family to face their circumstances without him.

For Aaliya's mother, this was another devastating reality to accept.

She had not imagined that one day she would have to raise her daughters while living separately from their father, even though they were still under the same roof.

The emotional burden was enormous.

She had to think about food, household expenses, education, and every little responsibility that came with raising three daughters. There was no certainty about what tomorrow would bring, but she had to keep moving forward.

And what about the girls?

They were children.

Children who should have been spending their days playing, laughing, making memories, and enjoying the innocence of childhood.

They should have been experiencing the warmth of a family without having to understand the complications of adult relationships.

But Aaliya and her sisters were growing up differently.

Their childhood was filled with situations they were too young to comprehend. They witnessed arguments, experienced emotional distance, and gradually became familiar with the absence of the security that children naturally expect from their parents.

For Aaliya, these experiences began creating a deep sense of fear.

She was becoming increasingly sensitive to everything happening around her. Every change in the household, every difficult conversation, and every painful moment left an impression on her young mind.

She often wondered what would happen next.

Would things ever become normal?

Would her family ever live together peacefully?

Would her mother finally be happy?

She had questions, but very few answers.

By this time, Aaliya had reached the fifth standard.

She was growing older, attending school, and gradually moving towards the dreams she had always carried. Yet, while other children were occupied with their studies, friendships, and childhood adventures, Aaliya was learning lessons that no textbook could ever teach.

She was learning about responsibility, disappointment, sacrifice, and the complicated realities of family life.

Again........A Mother's Tears

The decision to separate was not easy for anyone.

Aaliya's mother cried.

She cried over the life she had imagined but never received. She cried over the responsibilities she had to carry alone. She cried because she knew her daughters deserved a childhood far more beautiful than the one they were experiencing.

And her daughters cried too.

They could not fully understand why their family had become divided. They could not understand why their father preferred to remain with the other members of the household rather than live with them.

All they knew was that something important had changed.

The feeling of having a complete family was slowly disappearing from their lives.

Aaliya watched her mother struggle and tried, in her own little way, to understand everything.

She was still a child, but life was introducing her to emotions that even grown-ups sometimes struggle to understand.

Her mother had chosen to live separately because she wanted a better environment for her daughters.

But the question remained: how would she manage everything alone?

How would she protect their childhood?

How would she provide them with the education and opportunities they deserved?

And most importantly, how much more would she have to sacrifice?

Aaliya's journey was becoming increasingly difficult, but neither she nor her mother knew what was waiting around the corner.

The Beginning of Something Unforeseen

For a while, life continued in this divided arrangement.

The girls remained with their mother, trying to adjust to their new circumstances. Their mother continued doing whatever she could to keep the household running.

Aaliya, meanwhile, continued growing up.

She was still the same girl who wanted to study, explore the world, and make her mother proud. But somewhere inside her, the little girl who once believed everything would eventually become alright was beginning to understand how unpredictable life could be.

And then, something happened.

Something so unexpected that it would shake the entire foundation of Aaliya's story.

An incident that would change the direction of everything that had happened so far.

No one could have imagined what was about to unfold.

Not Aaliya.

Not her sisters.

Not even their mother.

Because sometimes, just when a family believes it has endured the worst, life brings an entirely unexpected chapter.

And this time, nothing would remain quite the same.

To be continued...

CHAPTER

Chapter Four: The Day Destiny Stood Before the Panchayat

Sometimes, the greatest battles are not fought between strangers. They are fought within families, behind closed doors, where the people who are supposed to protect one another become the reason for each other's suffering.

For Aaliya's mother, another painful chapter was about to begin.

She had already endured years of hardship. She had struggled to raise her daughters, fought for their education, and tried to create a peaceful environment for them despite the circumstances.

But just when she thought she had witnessed enough, an unexpected development shook her world.

Aaliya's paternal grandmother had begun searching for another marriage proposal for her son.

Yes, she wanted to find another woman for Aaliya's father.

And what made the situation even more painful was that Aaliya's father seemed willing to agree with the proposal.

Imagine the emotional burden of a woman who was already struggling to maintain her household, raise three daughters, and protect her dignity, only to discover that her husband and his family were considering bringing another woman into his life.

For Aaliya's mother, this was not simply another family disagreement.

It was a moment that demanded a decision.

She understood that remaining silent would only allow the situation to become more complicated. She had spent years compromising, adjusting, and enduring circumstances that had gradually taken away her peace.

But this time, she decided to stand up for herself.

She decided to take a major step.

A Woman Who Refused to Remain Silent

In their community, serious family disputes were often brought before the Panchayat — a gathering of respected elders and influential members of the community who would listen to both sides and attempt to reach a decision.

Aaliya's mother decided to call a Panchayat.

But even arranging such a gathering was another struggle.

The Gathering

By this time, Aaliya had reached the sixth standard.

On one side stood Aaliya's mother, a woman who had spent years enduring difficulties and was now determined to speak about her circumstances.

On the other side stood Aaliya's father and his family, with their own position and expectations.

The atmosphere surrounding the matter was tense.

For Aaliya's mother, this gathering represented much more than a discussion between two families. It was an opportunity to finally have her voice heard.

For her daughters, however, the consequences could be life-changing.

Yet the future of their family was now being discussed in front of a gathering of people.

What would happen to their marriage?

Would the two separate paths finally become permanent?

Would Aaliya's mother receive the decision she had been waiting for?

Nasir's Decision

But Nasir remained stubborn.

He insisted that he wanted a divorce and did not appear willing to reconsider his position.

You will have to raise them and provide for them. You cannot simply walk away from everything. Think about what you are doing. This decision may create even greater difficulties for you."

The Agreement

After a long discussion, the elders suggested a possible arrangement.

Nasir was advised to continue living with his wife and daughters while also maintaining his relationship and responsibilities towards his parents.

He was expected to find a balance between his own family and his parents rather than allowing one relationship to destroy another.

Aaliya was growing up in the middle of it all.

What happens when a little girl begins to associate home with uncertainty rather than comfort?

What happens when the people who are supposed to provide security become the reason a child constantly worries about tomorrow?

She wanted to give her sisters a better future.

The Anger Behind Closed Doors

Aaliya's personality had changed considerably.

The girl who once tried to understand everyone had become distant. She no longer felt comfortable sharing her thoughts with people. Her patience had diminished, and her words often carried the weight of accumulated frustration.

She still wanted to make something of her life.

But she was tired of asking.

This time, she decided to find another way.

A Dream Beyond the Walls

Aaliya began preparing for NEET through Physics Wallah (PW). Online lectures became an important part of her daily routine. She studied concepts, made notes, revised chapters, and tried to understand difficult topics on her own.

Physics often tested her patience. Some concepts took hours to understand, while certain numerical problems made her question whether she was progressing quickly enough.

Chemistry brought its own challenges, and Biology required consistent revision.

There were days when she felt overwhelmed by the enormous syllabus. Sometimes, she would complete a lecture only to realize that she still had several questions left unanswered.

But she kept going.

Her room became her study space. Her books, notebooks, and phone became her constant companions. She learned to make the most of the resources available to her rather than waiting for the resources she had never received.

She was not preparing merely to secure admission into a medical college.

She had a deeper reason.

She wanted to leave behind the circumstances that had made her feel trapped for so many years. She wanted to build a future where her education, decisions, and opportunities would not depend entirely on someone else's willingness to support her.

Aaliya often reminded herself:

Once I qualify NEET, I will create a different life for myself. I cannot remain trapped in these circumstances forever.

The Battles Behind the Books

However, preparing for NEET was not simply a matter of watching lectures and completing chapters.

There were emotional battles, too.

At home, disagreements and disturbances sometimes interrupted her studies. There were moments when she desperately needed a peaceful environment but could not find one. On certain days, she had to put aside her books because the atmosphere around her became too difficult to ignore.

She also struggled with the pressure of preparing without the guidance she believed she needed.

Whenever she found a topic particularly difficult, she wished she had someone who could explain it to her personally. She watched lectures again, searched for explanations within her study material, and attempted questions until she understood them.

Some days were productive.

Others ended with unfinished targets and frustration.

But she refused to let a difficult day convince her that she was incapable.

The most painful part was that the person whose support she had once wanted most was still absent from her academic journey.

Nasir knew that Aaliya was preparing for a major examination, yet the encouragement she had hoped for never came.

She no longer expected it.

She had stopped waiting for him to become the father she had once imagined.

A Promise to Herself

As the examination approached, Aaliya's determination became even stronger.

She had made a promise that went beyond becoming a doctor.

Whether she qualified NEET or not, whether she eventually became a doctor or chose another path, she would not return to the relationship she once shared with Nasir.

She had made that decision after years of disappointment.

She imagined a day when she might achieve something remarkable. Perhaps one day, Nasir would introduce her proudly as his daughter, a doctor. Perhaps he would finally recognize her abilities.

But Aaliya wondered why that recognition should matter only after success.

Where had he been when she needed tuition?

Where had his encouragement been when she struggled with her studies?

Why had she needed to fight so hard for something that should have been supported?

She had no intention of allowing future success to erase those memories.

I wanted your support when I was struggling, not your pride after I succeed.

That thought stayed with her.

The Day of NEET

Finally, the day arrived.

It was an important day—not only because Aaliya was about to appear for one of the most significant examinations of her academic life, but because she had worked towards this moment through years of determination and sacrifice.

She prepared herself and went to the examination centre.

As she entered, she could feel the seriousness of the occasion. Around her were other students, each carrying their own expectations, preparation, and dreams. Some appeared confident, while others looked nervous.

Aaliya took her place.

The little girl who had once dreamed of becoming a doctor.

The student who had studied without the tuition she needed.

The daughter who had watched her family struggle.

The girl who had cried, become disappointed, and gradually learned to depend on herself.

All those memories seemed to accompany her into the examination hall.

Then she focused on the question paper.

She began answering.

Some questions were familiar, while others required careful thought. A few made her pause longer than expected. She managed her time, tried to remain composed, and continued working through the paper.

When the examination finally ended, she stepped outside with a mixture of exhaustion and relief.

She had done it.

After returning home, she reflected on the questions and her answers. She felt that her paper had gone well. For the first time in a long while, she allowed herself to feel hopeful.

But she did not place her expectations entirely on anyone else's opinion.

Whatever the result would be, she had given the examination her effort.

The Waiting

Days passed.

The result was approaching, and with every passing day, the tension grew.

Aaliya tried to remain calm, but she knew how much depended on this examination. Her future plans, her dream of entering medical college, and the possibility of finally moving towards an independent life were all connected to the outcome.

She wondered whether her hard work would be rewarded.

Would all those hours of studying finally lead somewhere?

Would she qualify?

And if she did, would the people who had never supported her suddenly begin to celebrate her achievements?

Aaliya had no answers.

She only knew that she had reached this point through her own determination.

Then came the day she had been waiting for.

The NEET result was about to be announced.

Aaliya sat with her thoughts, knowing that the next few moments could change the direction of her life.

Would the result bring her closer to the white coat she had dreamed of wearing since childhood?

Or was destiny preparing another unexpected turn?

Life at AIIMS Rishikesh introduced Aaliya to an entirely different world.

Physiology helped her understand how its different systems functioned, while Biochemistry brought another level of scientific detail.

Aaliya had to keep learning, adapting, and growing.

After completing her academic and clinical training requirements, Aaliya entered the compulsory rotating internship that forms an essential part of medical education.

The Dream Had Come True

Turkey.

The girl who had once struggled to imagine a peaceful future was now standing beneath a sky of lights and surrounded by roses, having just said yes to a new possibility.

But was this the beginning of the beautiful future she had always dreamed of?

Only destiny knew.

To be continued…

Chapter Twenty-Seven: The Kind of Love She Had Never Known

Sometimes, life changes not through one extraordinary event, but through a thousand little moments that slowly find their way into someone's heart.

For Aaliya, everything began to feel different after that evening beneath the roses.

She had accepted Çağrı's proposal, and although she was still trying to understand how quickly her life had taken this unexpected turn, one thing was certain: she had allowed someone to become an important part of her world.

And Çağrı seemed determined to make her feel that she mattered.

The Little Things That Meant Everything

Çağrı had a habit of checking on Aaliya throughout the day.

His messages often arrived without warning.

Have you eaten anything?

What are you doing right now?

Have you reached the university?

Are you tired?

Do you need anything?

Sometimes, Aaliya would look at her phone and find several messages from him.

One afternoon, while she was studying, her phone began ringing.

"Hello?"

"Finally! I've been trying to reach you."

Aaliya laughed.

"Çağrı, I was studying. I can't keep my phone in my hand all day."

"Alright, Doctor. But tell me something first. Have you eaten?"

She looked towards the clock.

"Not yet."

There was a brief silence.

"Aaliya!"

"What?"

"You've been studying for hours, and you haven't even eaten?"

"I'll eat in a little while."

"No. Not in a little while. Now."

She laughed at his seriousness.

"You're becoming very strict."

"Only when it comes to your health."

Aaliya shook her head, smiling.

"Fine. I'll eat."

"Good. And send me a message when you finish."

"Yes, sir!"

He laughed.

"Very funny."

For Aaliya, conversations like these became increasingly precious. They were ordinary questions, but nobody had ever made her feel that even the smallest details of her day deserved attention.

When She Wasn't Feeling Well

A few days later, Aaliya woke up feeling unwell. She had a headache and very little energy, but she still tried to continue with her university work.

When Çağrı called, he immediately noticed that something was different.

"Why does your voice sound like that?"

"Nothing. I'm just a little tired."

"Are you feeling alright?"

"Yes, I'm fine."

"Aaliya, I know when you're pretending to be fine."

She remained quiet.

"Do you have a headache?"

"A little."

His expression changed.

"Have you taken any rest? Have you spoken to someone about it?"

"It's nothing serious, Çağrı. Don't worry."

"I'm not asking you to worry me less. I'm asking you to take care of yourself."

He encouraged her to rest and make sure she received appropriate medical advice if she needed it. He also checked whether Aliza was around to help.

Later, Aliza brought Aaliya something warm to eat.

Aaliya looked at her phone again. There was another message from Çağrı.

Don't study tonight. Rest properly. Your books will still be there tomorrow.

She smiled.

For a moment, she felt an emotion she couldn't quite explain.

She was a doctor, someone who had spent years learning to care for others. Yet she had rarely experienced someone paying such thoughtful attention to her own well-being.

It wasn't the grand gestures that touched her most.

It was the fact that he remembered.

A Different Kind of Happiness

As the days passed, Çağrı became increasingly familiar with Aaliya's habits.

He learned that she sometimes forgot to eat when she was occupied with her studies. He noticed that she became quiet when something troubled her. He understood that she didn't always express what she needed.

And he never stopped asking.

One evening, they were sitting together at a café overlooking the beautiful streets of Istanbul.

Aaliya was looking through the window when Çağrı placed a cup of coffee in front of her.

"Here."

She looked at it.

"What's this?"

"Your coffee."

"I didn't ask for it."

"I know. But I remembered how you like it."

Aaliya looked at him, then at the cup.

"You remembered?"

"Of course. Do you think I forget everything you tell me?"

She smiled.

"Sometimes I think you notice things that even I don't notice about myself."

"Someone has to."

She laughed.

For a little while, they simply sat together, enjoying the evening.

Then Çağrı asked, "Tell me something. If you could go anywhere in the world right now, where would you go?"

Aaliya looked towards the city.

"Istanbul is already a dream come true. But there are so many places I still want to see."

"Then we'll see them."

She turned towards him.

"All of them?"

"Why not? We have time."

Aaliya smiled, but his words stayed with her.

For so long, she had imagined a future in which she would have to achieve everything alone. Now, for the first time, someone was speaking about the future as though her dreams belonged in it too.

The Girl Who Began Smiling Again

There was a time when Aaliya had felt disappointed with almost everyone around her.

Her childhood had taught her to expect very little from people. She had built walls around herself because trusting someone had once meant risking another heartbreak.

But Çağrı's presence gradually introduced her to a different experience.

He wanted to see her happy.

If she had a difficult day, he tried to make her laugh. If she was busy with university, he encouraged her. If she became quiet, he gave her space instead of demanding explanations.

Sometimes he would call simply to say:

"I was thinking about you. That's all."

And sometimes, when she asked why he was checking on her so frequently, he would reply:

"Because I want to know that you're alright."

Aaliya began smiling more often.

Aliza noticed the change before Aaliya herself did.

One afternoon, Aliza looked at her while she was reading a message on her phone.

"Someone seems very happy today."

Aaliya tried to hide her smile.

"Nothing like that."

"Oh, really? Then why have you been smiling at your phone for the last five minutes?"

"Aliza, stop it!"

Aliza laughed.

"I'm just saying. It's nice to see you happy."

Aaliya looked down at her phone again.

Perhaps Aliza was right.

Aaliya's World Begins to Change

Gradually, Çağrı became an important part of her everyday life.

She began sharing little details with him—what happened at the hospital, what she had studied, what made her laugh, and even the smallest things that irritated her.

She would sometimes send him photographs of the places she visited, and he would respond with questions or suggestions about where they should go next.

He often spoke about places he wanted to show her.

"We should visit the seaside this weekend."

"Maybe."

"Maybe? That's not an answer."

"Alright, yes. Happy now?"

"Very."

Their conversations were filled with laughter, teasing, and small disagreements that never lasted long.

And somewhere along the way, Aaliya began to realize how deeply attached she had become.

She had once believed that happiness was something she would have to create entirely by herself. She had worked hard to become independent, to build a future beyond the painful memories of her childhood.

She still valued that independence.

But now, she had someone beside her who wanted to share her happiness rather than take away her strength.

Çağrı had become a special part of her life.

Perhaps she was falling in love more deeply than she had ever imagined possible.

And perhaps the most beautiful part was that she no longer felt she had to hide every emotion behind silence.

One evening, while they were talking, Çağrı looked at her and said,

"You know something, Aaliya? I like seeing you smile."

She smiled back.

"And I like that you always find a reason to make me smile."

He looked at her for a moment.

"Then I'll keep finding reasons."

Aaliya lowered her eyes, unable to hide her happiness.

For someone who had spent so much of her life feeling forgotten, being remembered in the smallest ways felt extraordinary.

She had finally begun to believe that she deserved kindness, patience, and affection.

And as the days passed, her world seemed to revolve around a new kind of happiness.

She didn't know what destiny had planned for them.

For now, she only knew that she was happy.

And sometimes, when a person has waited a lifetime to feel loved, even the simplest moments become unforgettable.

Chapter Twenty-Eight: A Thousand Memories and a Promise of Care

Love is not always expressed through extraordinary words or expensive gifts. Sometimes, it reveals itself through the smallest gestures—a worried phone call, a gentle question, or someone remembering to ask whether you have eaten.

For Aaliya, Çağrı's affection was becoming something she experienced every day.

He had gradually become part of her routine, someone she could share her happiest moments with and someone she could turn to when life felt difficult.

But one morning, something changed.

When Aaliya Fell Ill

Aaliya had been feeling unwell for a couple of days. What initially seemed like ordinary tiredness gradually became more troublesome. She felt weak and had little energy to carry on with her usual routine.

Aliza noticed that she wasn't herself.

"You should rest, Aaliya. You've been pushing yourself too much."

"I'm alright. I just need a little sleep."

But when Çağrı called that afternoon, he immediately noticed her weak voice.

"Aaliya, what's wrong? You don't sound well."

"Nothing much. I'm just feeling a little sick."

"A little sick? Have you taken proper rest?"

She smiled faintly.

"You're starting your questions again."

"And I'll keep asking until you tell me you're taking care of yourself."

He encouraged her to rest and seek appropriate medical attention rather than ignore her symptoms. He also checked that Aliza was there to help her.

Throughout the day, his messages continued.

Have you eaten something?

Are you feeling any better?

Please don't spend the entire day studying.

Let me know if you need anything.

At one point, Aaliya called him.

"Çağrı?"

"Yes, I'm here."

"Why are you worrying so much?"

There was a brief pause.

"Because you're important to me, Aaliya. I don't like knowing that you're unwell."

She didn't immediately respond.

It was a simple sentence, but it touched something deep inside her.

When Çağrı later visited, he made sure not to overwhelm her. He asked whether she needed anything, spoke with Aliza about how she was doing, and stayed only as long as Aaliya felt comfortable.

Before leaving, he looked at her and said,

"Promise me you'll rest."

"I promise."

"And no studying until you're feeling better."

She laughed softly.

"Now you're giving orders?"

"I'm making a request, Doctor."

"Alright. I promise."

He smiled.

"Good. Get well soon."

A Little Better, A Little Happier

Over the next few days, Aaliya gradually recovered.

Her energy returned, her usual smile reappeared, and she began looking forward to spending time outside again.

Çağrı noticed the improvement immediately.

"Someone sounds much better today."

"Because someone has finally stopped giving me lectures."

He laughed.

"Very funny. Anyway, I have a plan."

Aaliya became curious.

"What plan?"

"I'm taking you out."

"Where?"

"That's a surprise."

"Çağrı!"

"All you need to know is that we're going on a picnic."

Aaliya smiled.

"A picnic?"

"Yes. You've spent enough time indoors. You deserve a beautiful day outside."

She agreed.

And so, they began planning their little outing.

A Day Away from Everything

The day of the picnic arrived with beautiful weather.

The sky was clear, a gentle breeze moved through the trees, and the surroundings were filled with the peaceful atmosphere of a perfect afternoon.

Çağrı had arranged everything thoughtfully. There was a picnic blanket, a selection of food, drinks, and a beautiful place where they could spend the day without distractions.

When Aaliya arrived, she looked around in admiration.

"Çağrı! You arranged all this?"

He smiled.

"Of course. Did you think I was bringing you here without a plan?"

She laughed.

"I didn't expect this much."

"Then I'm glad I surprised you."

They settled down and began enjoying their afternoon.

They talked about university, their childhood memories, their dreams, and the places they hoped to visit together. Sometimes they laughed so much that they forgot what they had originally been discussing.

Çağrı took out his phone.

"Come on. Let's take a picture."

Aaliya smiled.

"Again? How many photographs are you going to take?"

"As many as I want. These are memories."

He captured a photograph of them together.

Then another.

And another.

Some photographs were carefully posed, while others captured their spontaneous laughter. They took pictures of the scenery, the food, the flowers, and the beautiful afternoon surrounding them.

At one point, Aaliya looked at one of their photographs and laughed.

"Look at your expression!"

"What's wrong with my expression?"

"You look so serious!"

"That's because you weren't cooperating with the photographer."

She laughed even harder.

"You're impossible!"

"Yet you agreed to come on a picnic with me."

"Unfortunately."

He pretended to look offended, making her laugh again.

For Aaliya, these moments felt precious.

She had spent so many years worrying about tomorrow that she had almost forgotten what it felt like to enjoy the present.

That afternoon, she wasn't thinking about examinations, family arguments, or painful memories.

She was simply Aaliya—laughing, taking photographs, and making memories in a city she had once only dreamed of visiting.

The Little Things He Always Asked

As their afternoon continued, Aaliya noticed something about Çağrı.

He never assumed that his feelings gave him the right to make decisions for her.

If he wanted to hold her hand, he asked.

If he wanted to sit closer, he paid attention to whether she was comfortable.

If he wanted to take a photograph, he checked with her first.

Even the smallest gestures came with consideration.

Once, while they were walking together, he gently extended his hand.

"May I?"

Aaliya looked at his hand and smiled.

"Yes."

He held hers, and they continued walking.

What made this gesture special was not simply that he held her hand. It was that he never treated her comfort as something unimportant.

He understood that affection should never become pressure.

Aaliya had experienced situations in which her feelings were ignored. With Çağrı, she was discovering something different: a person could care deeply without making her feel uncomfortable or taking away her freedom.

He never wanted her to feel obligated to accept anything simply because they were together.

And Aaliya noticed.

A Memory She Wanted to Keep Forever

As the afternoon slowly came to an end, they sat together, watching the changing colors of the sky.

Aaliya looked through the photographs on her phone.

"Look at these. We have so many pictures."

Çağrı glanced at her screen.

"Which one's your favorite?"

She showed him one photograph in which they were both laughing naturally.

"This one."

"Why?"

"Because neither of us was posing. We were just happy."

Çağrı looked at the photograph and smiled.

"Then we'll make many more memories like this."

Aaliya turned towards him.

"Promise?"

He nodded.

"Promise."

She rested her gaze on the scenery for a moment.

For someone who had once believed that happiness was something other people experienced, this day felt almost unreal.

Çağrı had become incredibly special to her. His care, patience, and thoughtful gestures had slowly helped her open a part of herself she had kept hidden for years.

He loved seeing her happy, and she had begun to look forward to every moment they spent together.

As the evening approached, they packed their things and prepared to leave.

Before getting into the car, Çağrı took one final photograph of the beautiful place.

"Another memory," he said.

Aaliya smiled.

"One of many."

They returned to Istanbul carrying photographs, laughter, and another beautiful day to remember.

But neither of them knew what awaited them next.

Sometimes, life allows people to experience extraordinary happiness just before presenting them with a challenge they never anticipated.

Aaliya believed that her life was finally moving towards the peaceful future she had always wanted.

She had her medical career, a new home in Istanbul, a wonderful friendship with Aliza, and Çağrı, who had become one of the most important people in her world.

Everything seemed to be falling into place.

But destiny had not revealed its next chapter yet.

And in Chapter Twenty-Nine, an unexpected twist is about to shake the entire story—an event that will change the direction of this book and leave Aaliya's world completely different.
